skeleton: gentle chubby Brachiosaurus standing on four pillar legs, three-quarter view facing left, its very long neck rising high to a small round head: root on the ground under the body; body (pivot over the legs) with belly squash, the body piece carrying the very base of the neck as a short stump with a round top; neck (lower half) on the stump and neckTop (upper half) on the neck, each piece drawn hanging so its base fades in over the part below (fadeTop), each joint's lower end a round knob hidden under the part above at any turn; head on neckTop (its own chin line, its bottom soft), face with eyes (the far one smaller, by the snout), brows and mouth; legFF/legBF (far legs, behind the body, shaded) and legFN/legBN (near legs, over the body with faded tops) at shoulders and hips; short tail behind the body, its root tucked under the body's soft back edge.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a gentle, chubby, sage-green Brachiosaurus standing on its four thick pillar legs, turned a little to the left, its very long neck rising high to a small round head. Draw this exact Brachiosaurus as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body: the big round chubby body with its cream chest and tummy and its darker green spots, turned as in image 1, without head, without legs and without tail: no legs, thighs or feet drawn on it, its underside one smooth rounded line from the chest to the back. At the front, where the long neck rises, the cream chest and the green shoulders carry on up only a little, into a short, wide stump of the neck's base, about half as tall as the head, ending in a full, smooth, rounded top with NO outline across it. At the back, the spotted back runs on smoothly into the very root of the tail and ends there in a soft edge cut straight down, with NO outline across it: no round bump, no stump, no line where the tail would join.
2. the lower half of the long neck, drawn UPSIDE DOWN (turned half a turn, as if hanging from its base): its thick base, where it grows out of the shoulders, at the TOP, a soft straight edge with NO outline across it; its narrower middle at the BOTTOM, a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it. The cream throat runs along one side and the spotted green back of the neck along the other, as in image 1; the drawing's dark outline runs only down its two long sides.
3. the upper half of the long neck, drawn UPSIDE DOWN the same way: its wider middle end at the TOP, a soft straight edge with NO outline across it; its narrow top end, just under the head, at the BOTTOM, a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it. The cream throat along one side and the spotted green back along the other; the dark outline only down its two long sides.
4. the head alone, without neck: the small round head with its rounded snout, its two little nostrils, its darker green spots and its rosy cheek, turned as in image 1, with a completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, no mouth and no mouth line, the snout and the cream jaw one smooth shape; keep the nostrils, the spots and the rosy cheek. Keep its dark outline over the top of the head, round the snout and along the jaw under the snout to the chin, as in image 1. From the chin round to the back of the head its bottom edge is soft, with NO outline: the cream throat and the green back of the neck simply stop there, just below the rosy cheek.
5. the far front leg: the leftmost leg of image 1, partly behind the cream chest, drawn whole from the top of its shoulder (normally hidden behind the chest) down to its round foot with its soft cream toenails, a thick, straight pillar as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.
6. the near front leg: the big pillar leg of image 1 under the chest, the second leg from the left, drawn whole from the top of its broad shoulder down to its round foot with its soft cream toenails, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.
7. the far back leg: the shorter leg of image 1 under the belly, between the two big near legs, mostly hidden there, drawn whole from the top of its thigh (normally hidden behind the belly) down to its round foot with its soft cream toenails, a thick, straight pillar; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.
8. the near back leg: the big leg of image 1 on the right, under the hip, drawn whole from the top of its big round thigh down to its round foot with its soft cream toenails, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.
9. the tail: the short, thick, spotted tail with its cream underside, curving up a little to its rounded tip as in image 1, drawn whole from its thick root (normally hidden inside the body) to the tip; its root a full, smooth, rounded end with NO outline across it.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or another part) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. Nothing sharp: no claws, no teeth. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a gentle, chubby, sage-green Brachiosaurus; image 2 shows the same Brachiosaurus cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the Brachiosaurus's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the Brachiosaurus in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2. Its small head is turned to the left: its far eye (on the left of image 1, near the snout) is smaller than its near eye (on the right of image 1). In image 1 both eyes look to the left: each big dark-brown iris sits towards the left of its eye, the white on its right.

Draw each piece on its own, upright, in five tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the far eye (the smaller eye, on the LEFT of image 1), six times:
1. as it is in image 1: a big dark-brown iris with a white sparkle, looking to the left.
2. wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, the dark-brown iris with a white sparkle, looking the same way.
3. closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, like an upside-down U.
4. sad: open and round, a soft brown iris with a white sparkle looking down and to the left, a thin shine of a welling tear along its bottom rim; no lid slanting across it.
5. crying: squeezed shut, a thick lid line as wide as the open eye, curving down at both ends like a little frown, and one small light-blue teardrop just below its outer (left) end.
6. gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line as wide as the open eye, with a few short lashes.
Row 2, the near eye (the bigger eye, on the RIGHT of image 1), the same six in the same order; open, it looks the same way as row 1, to the left, the iris towards the left of the eye; crying, its teardrop below its outer (right) end.
Row 3: 13. the far eyebrow (over the left eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 14. the same far eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (right) end. 15. the near eyebrow (over the right eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a thin dark-brown arch. 16. the same near eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (left) end.
Row 4, mouths, none with any teeth: 17. the mouth as it is in image 1: a long, thin, closed smiling line, gently curved, curling up into a smile at its right end. 18. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, rounded, the inside pink with a little pink tongue, no teeth. 19. the mouth open in a small round 'o', the inside pink. 20. the mouth in a small sad frown. 21. the mouth wide open in a big round 'O', a big sleepy yawn, the inside pink with a little tongue, no teeth. 22. the mouth sobbing: a small open downturned frown with a little pink inside.
Row 5: 23. the mouth closed and chewing: the smiling line squeezed shorter and a little wavy, its right end puffed up as if the cheek were full. 24. a small leafy sprig: a short green stalk with three soft, round, fresh green leaves, a mouthful the Brachiosaurus nibbles.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a gentle, chubby, sage-green Brachiosaurus with a very long neck; image 2 shows the same Brachiosaurus cut into puppet parts. Draw three more cut-out puppet parts of this exact Brachiosaurus on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in images 1 and 2, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, far apart on the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
1. the body: exactly the body of image 2 (the big round body with its cream chest and tummy, its darker green spots and the short wide stump of the neck's base at the front, ending in a soft rounded top with no outline), without head, neck, legs or tail. But at the back, the spotted back and the cream underside run on smoothly into the very root of the tail and end there in a soft edge cut straight down, with NO outline across it (the tail tucks under it): no round rump, no bump, no line where the tail would join. The drawing's dark outline runs only along the front of the chest, round the tummy and along the back, and stops at that soft cut.
2. the LOWER half of the long neck of image 1, drawn UPSIDE DOWN (its base at the top of the drawing): it is SHORT, only half of the neck of image 1, about as long as the head of image 1 is wide and not much longer than it is wide at its base. At the TOP its thick base, as wide as the neck where it rises from the shoulders in image 1, a soft straight edge with NO outline across it. At the BOTTOM its narrower middle end, a full, smooth half-circle with NO outline across it. The cream throat along its left side, the spotted green back of the neck along its right side; the dark outline only down its two long sides.
3. the UPPER half of the long neck of image 1, drawn UPSIDE DOWN the same way: just as SHORT, about as long as the head of image 1 is wide. At the TOP its middle end, as wide as the bottom end of part 2, a soft straight edge with NO outline across it. At the BOTTOM its narrow top end, as wide as the neck just under the head in image 1, a full, smooth half-circle with NO outline across it. The cream throat along its left side, the spotted green back along its right side; the dark outline only down its two long sides.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the brachiosaurus walks slowly along on its four big pillar legs, its long neck gently bobbing, then stops.
the brachiosaurus nods its little head yes, twice, slowly and kindly.
the brachiosaurus shakes its little head no, slowly, from side to side.
the brachiosaurus looks one way, then the other, high up on its long neck, then back.
the brachiosaurus laughs and laughs, its little head tipped up and its round tummy bouncing with giggles.
the brachiosaurus does a happy, heavy little dance, swaying its big body and long neck from side to side and swinging its tail.
the brachiosaurus talks, its mouth moving, its little head bobbing gently.
the brachiosaurus cries, its long neck drooping, little tears falling, its big tummy shaking with sobs.
the brachiosaurus gives a big slow yawn, closes its eyes and dozes off standing up, its long neck drooping, then wakes up, blinks and smiles.

pause.shows: the brachiosaurus fast asleep standing up, eyes shut, its long neck drooping

animations.description: the brachiosaurus shivers and trembles all over, cold or scared.
the brachiosaurus stretches its long neck up, up, up, as high as the treetops, then settles back down with a happy sigh.

pause.shows: the brachiosaurus reaching its long neck up high to the treetops

animations.description: the brachiosaurus munches a mouthful of leaves, chewing slowly, its cheeks moving, and smiles, very happy.
the brachiosaurus lowers its long neck slowly all the way down to the ground to sniff and drink, then lifts it back up high.

pause.shows: the brachiosaurus with its long neck lowered all the way to the ground, sniffing

animations.description: the brachiosaurus dips its little head and sniffs, sniff, sniff, then lifts it with a happy smile.
the brachiosaurus wags its short tail happily from side to side.
the brachiosaurus lifts one big front foot and sets it down with a gentle, heavy stomp and a little puff of dust, then smiles.
the brachiosaurus sways its long neck gently from side to side, humming a happy tune with its eyes closed.
